MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Aenima and Lateralus feel like natural next choices after 10.000 Days because I want more of Tool's heavy riffs, intricate rhythms, and immersive songs.",
    "American Idiot and The Young and the Hopeless fit the energetic, catchy guitar music I enjoyed in Chuck, giving me a lighter option that still has punch."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "X&Y and How to Dismantle An Atomic share a broad rock connection with my listening, but their melodic or anthemic sound does not satisfy my current appetite for heavier, more forceful music.",
    "Kid A's electronic atmosphere and The Piper at the Gates of Dawn's vintage psychedelia miss the particular kind of heaviness I want; experimentation alone is not what makes Tool appealing to me.",
    "The Marshall Mathers and No Strings Attached do not offer the guitar-driven sound I am looking for on this visit."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The choices seem to assume that broadly related rock albums will appeal equally, even though aggression, guitar weight, and rhythmic complexity matter a lot to me right now.",
    "Some choices feel connected mainly by their era rather than by the sound that draws me to my recent albums."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My latest listening to 10.000 Days makes further exploration of Tool especially appealing, alongside the heavier direction reflected in Ten Thousand Fists.",
    "My history includes both heavy music and accessible guitar rock, but the accessible side still needs energy and punch; a melodic sound by itself is not enough."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly understood my interest in energetic guitar music, but missed how strongly I currently favor heaviness and Tool's rhythmic complexity."
}
